explanation:
Read-only audit completed against pristine18.7, replay18.7 (including the uncommitted navigation repair), and pristine18.10; no builds, tests, provider requests, credential access, or edits were performed. The upgrade is not behaviorally equivalent: persistent-prefix and Codex effort protections require migration, and the baseline still has a concrete fork/prefix defect; the following family decisions and proposed probes are research recommendations, not exercised acceptance.

ROOT KEY: B=/tmp/omp-18100-audit-cd9kqmcj/replay-18.7.0/node_modules/@oh-my-pi; T=/tmp/omp-18100-audit-cd9kqmcj/pristine-18.10.0/node_modules/@oh-my-pi; P=/tmp/omp-18100-audit-cd9kqmcj/pristine-18.7.0/node_modules/@oh-my-pi.

FAMILY persistent-prefix-resume — REBASE/BLOCK until preserved. P→T session-context.ts changes only the readonly parameter of getLatestCompactionEntry; none of the local reconstruction protections is absorbed there. Retain durable eval reminders, retry/length/stall reminders, advertised model-agent tool surface, current-model system-prompt rebuilding, matched live/reconstructed interrupted-turn filtering, stable Juice placement, date/cwd anchors, and the uncommitted model/effort navigation repair. Exact ownership evidence is patches/.18.7.0-families/family-persistent-prefix-resume-v18.7.0.patch:170-418,724-1332. B agent-session.ts:11862-11900 confirms branch(entryId)/fork(entryId) still restore messages without persisting the current model/effort onto the truncated branch; T:11817-11925 retains this gap. A->B followed by branching before the B entry leaves the live agent on B but the child journal on A; buildSessionContext's explicit-default protection (T session-context.ts:305-341) then correctly refuses to infer B from later assistant replies, and fresh SDK restore chooses A (T sdk.ts:1997-2020). This is an inherited baseline defect, not a newly introduced upstream regression, and the current navigation-only repair does not close it. Minimal extension: apply the same durable selection snapshot policy to successful branch/fork-at-entry/branchFromBtw transitions, not merely navigateTree. Preserve ephemeral fallback semantics rather than converting every live model to default. T navigateTree:12350-12356 lacks the local repair, so upgrading without it also reintroduces the already-fixed navigation A/B drift. The serialized consequence is not merely a field mismatch: rebuilding a model-dependent system prompt, provider route, reasoning controls, and tool exposure against A changes the request prefix after a B continuation.

Selection semantics checked: T model-controls.ts:225-306 persists default/role choices and session-only temporary choices; temporary is durable in the journal even though settings are unchanged. EPHEMERAL_MODEL_CHANGE_ROLE is 'fallback' (B session-entries.ts:35); getRestorableSessionModels deliberately restores default for that role (T session-context.ts:132-148). That reversion is intentional and must not be reported as A/B loss. SDK explicit model options intentionally bypass session selection (T sdk.ts:1997-2000); explicit thinking option precedes journal selector, selector suffix, role default, model default and global default (2046-2109). Normalization/reclamping is intentional, as is auto reclassification (model-controls.ts:167-182). switchSession resolves saved model candidates, applies explicit overrides, and restores effort (T agent-session.ts:11512-11621); lack of an available model can produce a warned/allowed fallback or refusal, not an unconditional claim that B always restores. The source inspection does not establish provider-side cache hits.

FAMILY 0069-codex-effort-history-resume — REBASE, do not retire. B persists effortControl on the assistant native payload, clones the most recent matching successful branch snapshot before planning, and carries original request-level effort plus historical configuration_update positions. T openai-codex-responses.ts:1635-1655 instead uses process-local effortControls; T openai-configuration-update.ts:85-96 adds useful parentSessionId copy isolation, :100-107 releaseSession cleanup, and :160-206 minimized-effort planning. Port the durable history source without discarding these upstream additions; the state now requires sessionId, so the old zero-argument constructor patch is not source-compatible. Preserve branch-local snapshots, explicit model/api/provider matching, nonmutation of stored snapshots, and exclusion of error/aborted carriers and compact requests. The actual payload consumer was checked: T utils.ts:653-664 spreads the payload rather than rebuilding only items, while T session-manager.ts:3730-3742 and messages.ts:937-972 sanitize only GitHub Copilot. Thus ordinary Codex metadata can survive JSONL restoration, but it must be read by the new planner. Native items alone do not encode historical configuration_update items; those are injected separately by the effort planner. Parent-state cloning alone cannot repair cold resume because the parent map is also absent in a fresh process.

FAMILY 0017-openai-responses-native-replay-warm — REBASE/REDUCE rather than unconditionally replay the old one-line override. T openai-responses.ts:462 initializes nativeHistoryReplayWarmed to !model.compat.connectionBoundNativeHistory, whereas pristine18.7 initialized false and local 0017 set true. For ordinary self-contained native history, upstream now supplies the protected cold-start behavior. Preserve upstream's intentional connection-bound exception rather than force-warming it. The consumer is T:1583-1603: the flag gates both nativeHistory.replay and thinking signatures in buildResponsesInput. close() still clears the flag (475), matching the old patch's close behavior; it is not a new regression. Full retirement requires the parent to establish intended-provider configuration coverage and exercise ordinary OpenAI/Azure versus connection-bound Copilot. I do not claim unconditional behavioral equivalence from the similar initializer alone.

FAMILY 0050-session-history-preview — REBASE, substantial UI relocation. The old producer adds lastModel and role-aware tail scanning in B session-listing.ts:205-268,597; the old consumer adds the explicit read-only history overlay, controlled load/disposal, scrolling, first-two/last-ten text turns and selection callbacks (patches/0050-omp-session-history-preview.patch:198-242,275-410). T moves the picker into pi-tui/src/overlays/session-selector.ts and adds a native side preview (:124-152,1418-1422,1759-1828), but its 1200-character prompt/answer excerpt is not equivalent to the full scrollable history overlay. Rebase across the package boundary with an injected coding-agent history loader; do not add a pi-tui dependency back onto coding-agent session internals. Preserve ANSI/control sanitization, cancellation/disposal and enter/exit routing. Model labels from bounded prefix/tail windows remain weaker evidence than branch restoration; do not promote them to an authoritative resume oracle without resolving the active path. Acceptance should exercise the actual relocated UI consumer, not just presence of lastModel.

FAMILY 0072-session-pin-static-auth-ui — RETAIN/REBASE. T selector-controller.ts:178-181 still lazily requires pi-ai/index.js and registry/oauth/index.js, and the actual pin/login/logout callers remain at :2021,2160,2199,2268. The protection is not absorbed. Keep static pi-ai imports and lazy local UI components; audit any additional upstream auth-catalog exports through the same loader instead of mechanically replacing just two names. The NameTooLong shim failure is documented by the existing patch; no resolver failure was independently reproduced in this audit.

NEW ENTRYPOINT INTERACTIONS: T session-transfer.ts:1-14,119-123 defines archives as JSONL/artifacts/blobs only; :136-171 parses all arrived/departed/forked variants, and :175-178 persists their model-facing custom messages. These intentional appended notices are not unwanted prefix rewrites. However, replaying the local anchor mechanism onto this transfer path without including its out-of-journal map would lose every historical date/cwd stamp on another machine. T session-manager.ts:3960-4021 forkFrom preserves journal history, inherited cache key and native-payload sanitization, but cannot carry date-cwd-anchors stored outside artifacts. T full fork:2407-2446 mints a new session ID while retaining entries/cache key; the baseline anchor issue below therefore also applies to migration. T RPC fork is actually routed to session.fork(command.entryId,{requireIdle:true}) at modes/rpc/rpc-mode.ts:889-893 and maps busy failures at :1955-1970, so this is not an unhandled new command. T resetSessionContext:5884-5967 intentionally drops messages, rotates provider session state, appends reset_boundary and rebuilds the base prompt; session-context extracts model/effort settings before applying the reset boundary (:305-358), so reset is not itself evidence of A/B restoration loss.

HIGHEST-VALUE PARENT PROBES (proposed, not run): (1) One actual SDK/fresh-process fixture matrix: synthetic authenticated A/B model registry, explicit default A then durable default/temporary B, model-specific effort, navigateTree and branch/fork(entryId) before B, flush/dispose/reopen with no explicit model option; capture active model/effort and the actual serialized provider request. Include fallback-role and explicit CLI-option controls so intended overrides do not count as failures. (2) One intercepted actual Codex stream sequence: successful low-effort turn, high-effort turn, persist native assistant payload, then reconstruct in a fresh process and invoke the actual provider request builder; compare baseline reasoning.effort and complete input including update index/order, with side-request minimized-effort and branch snapshot controls. (3) One two-user-message date/cwd fixture through actual DateCwdReminderInjector plus SessionManager fork and, after migration, pack/unpack into an isolated second agent root; compare transformed historical messages before/after rather than only session fields. All fixtures should use private HOME/XDG, synthetic files/credentials and blocked external networking. Mandatory three exact policy greps were executed and matched. No runtime verification is claimed.

findings.title: Carry persisted reminder anchors across session forks
findings.body: CURRENT-BASELINE defect introduced by the persistent-prefix family: changing the session ID clears the anchor map and loads only the new ID's file. A full fork retains the same historical user messages but mints a new ID (session-manager.ts fork); no date-cwd anchor copying exists in the inspected coding-agent source. With two previously stamped user turns, the first post-fork provider transform consequently removes the old stamp from earlier turns and stamps only the newest eligible user turn, rewriting an already-sent prefix even though the transcript was cloned. Persist anchors with transferable session data or explicitly inherit/copy them at fork boundaries; the same migration must include session-transfer archives, which currently carry only JSONL, artifacts and blobs.

findings.title: Preserve durable Codex effort history when rebasing the planner
findings.body: MIGRATION loss, not a novel pristine-upstream regression: replacing the patched baseline with this planner drops 0069's branch-persisted effortControl snapshot. After a successful low-effort request followed by a high-effort request, a fresh process has no effortControls map entry; resolveOpenAIEffortControlState therefore initializes an empty state and planStableOpenAIEffort sends high as the request-level baseline without the historical low-to-high configuration_update. Both the request prefix and input sequence differ from the pre-resume request despite unchanged model/history. Restore the last matching successful assistant payload's durable state before planning, adapting its sessionId and preserving upstream side-request clone/release/minimized-effort behavior.
